register.name: Dominica Community Resilience Enhancement Project (DOMCREP)
register.detail: Green Climate Fund · SAP062 · Approved 30 October 2025 · in effect 17 March 2026 · grant · Caribbean Community Climate Change Centre
register.note: US$24,526,669 grant; about US$26 million in all with co-financing; completion due 17 March 2031
register.text: A Green Climate Fund grant for climate-resilient farming methods and technologies, stronger early warning systems and the retrofit of critical disaster management infrastructure, with the Caribbean Community Climate Change Centre as accredited entity. The Government of Dominica says it will support more than 520 farmers and agro-processors with climate-smart technology, irrigation and greenhouses, and that more than half of the total goes to agriculture and agro-processing. It serves the food standard, the furthest from reach.

register.name: Strengthening Fiscal and Climate Resilience Programmatic Development Policy Credit
register.detail: World Bank · IDA development policy credit · P508114 · release of 28 April 2025
register.note: Budget support tied to reforms in revenue, the financial sector, biodiversity and disaster preparedness
register.text: A World Bank development policy credit, an envelope of US$24 million from IDA, that supports Dominica in strengthening domestic revenue mobilisation and financial sector resilience, and in promoting biodiversity and disaster preparedness. The reforms it backs include higher excise taxes, stronger supervision of the AID Bank and the credit unions, the first marine protected area for sperm whale conservation and risk-based management of public buildings.

register.name: Disaster Vulnerability Reduction, third additional financing
register.text: Protection against storms, floods and landslides.

register.name: Emergency Agricultural Livelihoods and Climate Resilience, second additional financing
Geothermal Risk Mitigation, second phase
register.text: Drilling risk shared so that geothermal power can replace imported fuel.

register.name: Integrated physical adaptation and community resilience, enhanced direct access pilot (FP061)
register.detail: Green Climate Fund · Approved 1 March 2018 · grant · completion due 16 June 2027 · Department of Environment, Antigua and Barbuda
register.note: For Antigua and Barbuda, Dominica and Grenada together; Dominica’s share is not stated
register.text: A Green Climate Fund grant for three Eastern Caribbean island states, with the Department of Environment of Antigua and Barbuda as accredited entity. It offers small grants to community organisations and revolving loans to households and businesses so that buildings and infrastructure can withstand Category 5 hurricanes, and finances public infrastructure such as drainage and irrigation. It serves the shelter and water standards.

register.name: Policy-based loan for economic and climate resilience
register.detail: Caribbean Development Bank · announced 30 October 2026 · policy-based loan to the Government of the Commonwealth of Dominica
register.note: Reforms in public financial management, debt sustainability, financial sector stability and climate resilience
register.text: A US$10 million policy-based loan approved by the Caribbean Development Bank for the Government of the Commonwealth of Dominica, to back reforms that strengthen public financial management, improve debt sustainability, enhance financial sector stability and advance climate resilience. Stronger public finances are the base from which a state finances the seven standards.

register.name: Climate financing package, 2025
register.detail: Caribbean Development Bank · approved in 2025 · one of two packages of US$30M, with Saint Vincent and the Grenadines
register.note: Similar to the Bank’s environmental policy-based loan to Guyana; reforms in biodiversity, climate action and water
register.text: A financing package of US$30 million approved by the Caribbean Development Bank for Dominica in 2025, part of the Bank’s US$226.7 million of approvals for climate action that year. The Bank’s policy-based loans of 2025 support reforms in biodiversity conservation, climate action and water resource management, among other areas.

register.name: Debt financing for the Dominica Geothermal Plant Construction Project
register.detail: CARICOM Development Fund · financial close 1 September 2025 · part of a US$49.8M facility with the Caribbean Development Bank
register.note: With the CDB loan of US$34.8 million, it makes up the US$49.8 million debt facility
register.text: The CARICOM Development Fund’s contribution to a US$49.8 million debt financing facility, arranged with the Caribbean Development Bank, for the construction of Dominica’s geothermal power plant. The facility reached financial close on 1 September 2025. It serves the energy standard.

register.name: Loan for a 10 MW geothermal power plant
register.detail: Caribbean Development Bank · Approved 20 December 2024 · loan to the Geothermal Power Company of Dominica
register.note: 51% of a project of about US$68 million; the CARICOM Development Fund provides 22%
register.text: A Caribbean Development Bank loan to the Geothermal Power Company of Dominica to build a 10-megawatt geothermal power plant, drawing on resources from the Inter-American Development Bank, through the Green Climate Fund, and from the Government of Canada. The loan covers 51% of total project costs of about US$68 million; the CARICOM Development Fund provides 22% and the company’s equity the rest. It serves the energy standard.

register.name: Loubiere to Grand Bay road, rehabilitation
register.detail: UK Caribbean Infrastructure Fund · grant through the Caribbean Development Bank · 10.4 km of road and bridges · completion due December 2026
register.note: US$33.9 million; with a CDB loan of US$5.5 million and US$10.7 million from the Government of Dominica
register.text: A UK Caribbean Infrastructure Fund grant of £25.7 million (US$33.9 million), with a Caribbean Development Bank loan of US$5.5 million and US$10.7 million from the Government of Dominica, to upgrade 10.4 km of road and bridges between Loubiere and Grand Bay. The road is the key link between Roseau and the southern communities, and its construction is due to be completed in December 2026.

register.name: Strengthening Community Resilience within the Kalinago Territory (SCR-K)
register.detail: Government of India · India-UN Development Partnership Fund · UNDP · with the Kalinago Council
register.note: India’s total investment across its two projects in the Kalinago Territory
register.text: A project funded by the Government of India through the India-UN Development Partnership Fund and carried out by UNDP with the Government of Dominica and the Kalinago Council. It strengthens climate-resilient agriculture and food security, forest and watershed restoration and Indigenous tourism; in May 2026 backyard gardening kits were handed to vulnerable households. It serves the food standard.

register.name: Smart Sustainable Agriculture and Agro-Processing for Climate Resilience (ESSAA-1)
register.detail: Government of Italy · UNDP · October 2024 to March 2028 · Phase 1
register.note: Phase 1 budget of US$724,172.85, for a community-owned agro-processing centre co-designed with farmers
register.text: A UNDP project funded by the Government of Italy for smart, sustainable agriculture and agro-processing in Dominica. It is co-designing an Agro-Processing Technology Centre with farmers, beginning with more than 40 farmers of the Grand Bay Farmers Cooperative. It serves the food standard.

items.name: The Diaspora

items.text: Citizens abroad send home a steady share of the economy: a flow that can back long-term finance.
items.alt: A passenger ferry at the harbour quay in Dominica at dusk, with waterfront lights and dark green mountains behind.

items.name: The Farmland
items.label: Of the land in agriculture, 2023
items.text: Land that can feed the nation and earn abroad, valued and financed against its harvest.
items.alt: Small hillside farms in Dominica with banana plants and terraced plots of crops, below misty forested mountains.

items.name: The People
items.label: Citizens, 2025
items.text: 17.6% are under fifteen: the workforce and the market of the next generation.
items.alt: A street in Roseau, Dominica, lined with colourful Creole houses with balconies, green hills behind and people in the distance.

items.name: Dominica Essential Oils and Spices Cooperative
items.text: A cooperative of Dominica’s essential oil and spice producers. After it reported a slowdown in bay oil exports, the national export agency bought 3,094 pounds of bay oil from 78 farmers by February 2024, with World Bank financing, to support their livelihoods.

items.name: National Co-operative Credit Union
items.text: A member-owned credit union formed in 2010 by the merger of five credit unions, with more than 54,000 members and branches that include Castle Bruce and La Plaine. It describes itself as the largest credit union in Dominica and the wider Eastern Caribbean.
